title: Karwa Chauth 2025 Fasting Rules | Sargi Ritual & Fast Breaking Guide | Lifestyle News - News18
text: Karwa Chauth Fasting Rules: Karwa Chauth is one of the most cherished festivals among Hindu women, celebrated with devotion, traditions and rituals that have been carried on for centuries. The festival is dedicated to Goddess Parvati. Married women seek her blessings for marital bliss, prosperity and the long life of husbands. In 2025, Karwa Chauth will be observed on Friday, October 10. ALSO READ: Karwa Chauth 2025: Date, Moonrise Time, Muhurat In USA, UK And Canada According to the Purnimanta calendar followed in North India, the Chaturthi Tithi will begin at 10:54 PM on October 9 and end at 7:38 PM on October 10, making this day spiritually significant for married women across the country. Traditionally, the fast of Karwa Chauth is undertaken by married women who pray for the long life, health and well-being of their husbands. Women observe a strict day-long fast that is unique because most do not consume even a drop of water until the moonrise. ALSO READ: Karwa Chauth 2025: First Karva Chauth? Tips, Mistakes To Avoid And How To Make It Special Over time, however, customs have evolved. Today, some husbands also join their wives in fasting as a gesture of love and support. Even unmarried women, particularly in modern times, observe Karwa Chauth with the hope of finding a suitable life partner. This growing inclusivity shows how the festival has adapted while still holding deep emotional and cultural value. Karwa Chauth is not only about fasting but also about celebrating love and togetherness through meaningful traditions. Women begin their day before sunrise, dressing up in festive attire and applying mehendi. They eat Sargi at the beginning of the day. Sargi is one of the most beloved traditions of Karwa Chauth. ALSO READ: Karwa Chauth 2025: Puja Samagri List And Step-By-Step Ritual Guide This pre-dawn meal, prepared lovingly by mothers-in-law, includes a mix of sweet and savoury dishes that provide strength for the long day of fasting. The thali often contains pheni or meethi seviyan, dry fruits, mathri, parathas, fruits, coconut, sweets and a warm drink such as tea or juice. The ritual of eating Sargi strengthens the bond between a woman and her mother-in-law, while also symbolising blessings and prosperity for the couple’s married life. Throughout the day, women are encouraged to avoid household chores and focus instead on prayers, adornment and positive energy. As part of the customs, sharp objects such as knives and scissors are avoided. Meals that include onion and garlic are strictly prohibited. Harmony and patience are emphasized and women are expected to avoid conflicts or arguments since the festival symbolises love, unity and respect in marriage. Karwa Chauth is also associated with the beautiful ritual of Solah Shringar, which involves sixteen adornments that symbolise a woman’s love and respect for her marriage. These include sindoor, bangles, mehendi, kajal, necklaces, earrings, payal, toe rings, perfume, hair decorations and other traditional ornaments that transform the occasion into a grand celebration. As evening approaches, women prepare their pooja thali with essentials such as a decorated diya, lota, sweets and matthri. This thali plays a vital role in the final ritual of breaking the fast. The most anticipated moment of Karwa Chauth comes with the appearance of the moon. Dressed in their bridal best with mehendi and jewellery, women first offer prayers to Goddess Parvati and Lord Shiva before beginning the ritual. As the moon rises, they gaze at it through a sieve or channi and then look at their husband’s face through the same sieve. Water from the lota is offered in the moon’s direction along with small offerings like matthri. The husband then plays an important role in completing the ritual by giving his wife the first sip of water and a morsel of food, officially breaking her fast. Afterward, the family comes together to share a light meal, often including fruits, yogurt or simple, healthy dishes to ease digestion after a day of abstinence. Spicy and oily foods are avoided to ensure comfort after fasting.
